definitions.explanation: A person who acts foolishly or lacks good judgment. Somewhat literary or dramatic in tone, often found in stories, proverbs, and formal criticism.

examples.japanese: この{愚|おろ}か{者|もの}め！
{自分|じぶん}の{過|あやま}ちに{気|き}づかない{愚|おろ}か{者|もの}だ。
examples.english: He's a fool who doesn't notice his own mistakes.

examples.japanese: {歴史|れきし}から{学|まな}ばない{者|もの}は{愚|おろ}か{者|もの}と{呼|よ}ばれても{仕方|しかた}がない。
examples.english: Those who don't learn from history can't complain about being called fools.

notes:
Compound of {愚|おろ}か (foolish) + {者|もの} (person). Has a literary or dramatic quality — more likely heard in period dramas, stories, or solemn pronouncements than in casual conversation.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {愚|おろ}か{者|もの}め: "you fool!" (with contemptuous め particle)
- {愚|おろ}か{者|もの}と{呼|よ}ばれる: to be called a fool

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ばか: idiot (the most common everyday word; can be affectionate)
- あほ: fool (Kansai dialect equivalent of ばか; can also be affectionate)
- {愚|おろ}かな: foolish (the adjective form; modifies actions or decisions)
- {間抜|まぬ}け: dunce, blockhead (focuses on cluelessness)
